source.section: PDF p.46 Form 39R instructions Line 10; Form 40 lines 7-11, 12a, 15-20, 26 (PDF p.29-30); instructions PDF p.10-11 Standard Deduction Worksheet lines 1-6 and Line 20 worksheet lines 1-5; PDF p.13-14 Line 43 and Food Tax Credit Worksheet; PDF p.12 Line 31; record brackets and base.deductions cites

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 40,000.00 + dividends 5,000.00 + short-term gains 5,000.00 + long-term gains 20,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 38,500.00 (the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 40 (filing status married filing jointly): line 7 federal AGI 70,000.00. Line 8 additions 0.00; line 9 = 70,000.00 + 0.00 = 70,000.00. Form 39R Part B line 7 Social Security and railroad benefits included in federal income = 0.00 + 0.00 = 0.00. Line 8: no qualifying retirement benefits, line 8f 0.00. Line 18 health insurance premiums: none in the inputs, 0.00. Line 24 total subtractions = 0.00 + 0.00 = 0.00. Form 40 line 10 0.00; line 11 total adjusted income = 70,000.00 - 0.00 = 70,000.00. Line 12a boxes checked 0. Standard Deduction Worksheet: line 1 31,500.00; line 4 31,500.00; line 5 0 x 1,600.00 = 0.00; line 6 31,500.00. Line 15 0.00 (no Schedule A); line 16 31,500.00. Line 17 = 70,000.00 - 31,500.00 = 38,500.00. Line 18 federal Form 1040 lines 13a and 13b taken as 0.00; line 19 Idaho taxable income 38,500.00. Line 20 worksheet: line 1 38,500.00; line 2 9,622.00; line 3 = 28,878.00; line 4 at 5.3%; line 5 tax = 28,878.00 x 5.3% = 1530.534, to the cent 1,530.53 (the return rounds to whole dollars, PDF p.8, and shows 1,531; expected keeps the formula). Lines 21-24 credits 0.00; line 25 0.00; line 26 1,530.53. Food Tax Credit Worksheet (Form 40 line 43): 2 x 155.00 = 310.00. State income tax = 1,530.53 - 310.00 = 1,220.53. Line 31 Permanent Building Fund tax 10.00 is on the return but the projection does not charge it (approximations). The inputs do not say what was sold. Stock gains don't qualify for line 10 (PDF p.46), so the return matches the projection; a gain on qualified Idaho property would take the 60% deduction on the return, and the projection taxes it in full (approximations).
accepted_approximations: Gains on qualified Idaho property are taxed in full; 60% is deductible.
The Permanent Building Fund tax of 10 a return (Form 40 line 31) is not charged.
